content: Eluxadoline is a medication used to treat irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea (IBS-D). It works by slowing down the movement of the gut, which helps reduce diarrhea. This medication should be taken orally with food, typically twice a day, as directed by your doctor. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, response to treatment, and any other medications you may be taking. It is important to inform your doctor and pharmacist about all the products you use, including prescription drugs, nonprescription drugs, and herbal products. Do not increase your dose or use this medication more frequently or for a longer duration than prescribed, as this will not improve your condition faster and may increase the risk of side effects. To achieve the best results, use this medication regularly. If you are also taking loperamide to control diarrhea, avoid taking it on a regular schedule to prevent constipation. However, it may be used occasionally for severe diarrhea if needed. Eluxadoline may sometimes cause addiction, especially if you have a history of substance use disorder (e.g., overuse of or addiction to drugs or alcohol). To minimize the risk of addiction, take this medication exactly as prescribed. Common side effects of eluxadoline include constipation, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and drowsiness. If any of these effects persist or worsen, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but may occur. If you experience symptoms of a severe allergic reaction, such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek medical attention immediately. Eluxadoline may interact with other medications, potentially altering how they work or increasing the risk of serious side effects. It is essential to keep a list of all the products you use and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Avoid coadministration with drugs that cause constipation, as this may increase the risk of severe constipation-related complications, such as intestinal obstruction, perforation, or fecal impaction. Patients should be aware of the risk of sphincter of Oddi spasm, which may present as acute worsening of abdominal pain. If symptoms suggestive of this condition occur, such as severe abdominal pain, therapy should be discontinued immediately, and medical attention should be sought. Additionally, there is an increased risk of pancreatitis, particularly in patients with excessive alcohol use. Patients with a gallbladder should have their alcohol intake evaluated before starting therapy and should avoid chronic or acute excessive alcohol use during treatment. In postmarketing experience, serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported. Some of these reactions occurred after the first or second dose of treatment. Patients should discontinue therapy and seek medical attention immediately if they experience symptoms suggestive of a hypersensitivity reaction. Eluxadoline has not been studied in pregnant women, and it is unknown if it is distributed in human breast milk. However, it has been found to be secreted in rat milk. When considering the use of this medication during breastfeeding, weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother’s clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant. This medication should be stored at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it in a secure place to prevent theft, misuse, or abuse. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. If a dose is missed, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Patients should be instructed to stop therapy and contact their healthcare provider if they experience severe constipation lasting more than four days. Additionally, patients should be monitored for new or worsening abdominal pain that may radiate to the back or shoulder, with or without nausea and vomiting, as these symptoms may indicate pancreatitis. This medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages, and discuss with your doctor if you are using marijuana (cannabis). Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
